gaps.note: The overhead is O((eK)^tau+1) with K<=d^c<=e^{c/beta}, i.e. O(e^{tau(1+c/beta)}). That is O(e^lambda) only if tau(1+c/beta)<lambda, which the paper requires (lines 2398-2399 and 2414-2415) but the page omits; max{tau,sigma}<lambda<1 alone does not give it. The page also never states K=floor(d^c).

The page never states the edge identity that this recipe implements (frame change = P_M (prod C_{e_j}^{eta_j}) P_M^{-1}, paper eq. phase-edge-coordinate, lines 1855-1862), never defines X_v or C_v = aI+bX_v, and never explains the column vectors (x_{1,j},...,x_{m,j}) of the m slots on which P_M acts. The cited conjugation identity is thus not tied to the claim that follows.

gaps.quote: Applying $C$ individually to the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks makes their bits a row index
gaps.note: This requires D>q_0; the paper (lines 2313-2316) treats D<=q_0 separately by applying individual C kernels throughout, at cost O(V log d). The page states the row construction without that hypothesis and never explains why the row index range is large enough or why the cost of this preprocessing is within the bound.

gaps.quote: leaves add $O(\gamma^ju)\le O(e^\sigma u^{1-\sigma})\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)}).$
gaps.note: u and j are not defined on the page (paper lines 2421-2430: u=e/m^j<d^beta active chunks per leaf after j levels), so the reader cannot check the two inequalities, which use gamma^j<=m^{j sigma}=(e/u)^sigma and u<d^beta.

The page never says that the remaining D-q_0 chunks are written in base m and split into at most (m-1)(1+floor(log_m d)) consecutive pieces of m^j chunks (paper lines 2432-2436), which is where the log(2d) factor comes from. The cited result cannot be followed without it.

The value lambda'=1-2^{-54} depends on the fixed choices tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, beta=1/2, c=2^{-56}, lambda=1-2^{-52} (paper lines 4010-4026), none of which except beta appears on the page, so the reader cannot check that max{lambda,sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda'<1 holds. 's/W<m^sigma' alone does not give this value.

The page never says what A(e) or a chain is, nor derives the recurrence: the constant E=64(W+m+1)^3 comes from counting scalar gates (at most 12W gates, 2W^2 operations each), inverse-child and bank corrections (4s+4W+4) in paper lines 2490-2509, none of which is given. The recurrence has to be taken on trust.

sx+E<=(s+E)x holds only for x>=1 (paper line 2524); the page omits the hypothesis. The step to A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} also needs the depth k<=ceil(log_m d) of the recursion, e<=d, and B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^{log_m B}<=B^2 d^nu (paper lines 2523-2534), none of which is given.

C_0 and C_1 are never given. The bound A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} covers one group of e axes only; the paper (lines 2536-2560) adds the concatenated pieces (8mB^2 d^{nu+2}), preprocessing kernels, the outer diagonals and the scalar b^D to reach C_0=128mB^2, C_1=max{20,nu+3}. The page's Delta is therefore not shown to dominate the operation count.

gaps.quote: After $\ell$ operations a value lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell$
gaps.note: This holds only for values obtained from inputs in the unit disk lying on the grid 2^{-p}Z[i] (paper lines 2562-2565, by induction on depth); the page states it with no starting hypothesis and for 'operations' rather than depth along a dependency chain.

gaps.quote: row sums multiply under tensor products
gaps.note: The conclusion is about absolute row sums. Ordinary row sums also multiply under tensor products, but the second row of H_0 has sum 0, so they would not give 1. The correct statement is that the absolute row sum of H_0 is 1 for each row (|1/2|+|+-1/2|) and absolute row sums multiply, so every row of H_0^{(x)D} has absolute row sum one (paper line 2751).
